subQuestions.questionText:
Refer to sketches A and B based on the influence of anticyclones in South Africa.

Sketch A shows typical ... conditions.

A summer
B spring
C winter
D autumn

The low-pressure system in sketch B forms due to ... over the land.

A low evaporation
B intense heating
C cold dense air
D heavy rainfall

... is the concept used to describe the elongation of the isobars associated with the South Atlantic anticyclone in sketch B.

A Backing
B Divergence
C Ridging
D Convergence

The anticyclones in sketch A and B change their positions seasonally because of the ...

A rotation of the Earth.
B frictional drag.
C shifting of the ITCZ.
D Coriolis force.

The South Indian anticyclone in sketch B is likely to feed more moisture over the east coast in comparison with sketch A because it ...

A is a blocking high.
B has a larger fetch (distance).
C diverges dry air.
D has a smaller fetch (distance).

The low-pressure system in sketch A will move in a ... direction.

A northerly
B westerly
C easterly
D southerly

Berg winds are most likely to develop in sketch A because of the presence of the ... and ...

(i) Kalahari anticyclone
(ii) coastal low
(iii) South Indian anticyclone
(iv) heat low

A (i) and (ii)
B (ii) and (iii)
C (i) and (iv)
D (iii) and (iv)

The inversion layer that forms over the escarpment in sketch B will favour the formation of ... and ...

(i) frost
(ii) rainfall
(iii) fog
(iv) hail

A (i) and (ii)
B (i) and (iii)
C (ii) and (iv)
D (iii) and (iv)

Occurs during the day due to insolation.

A Sketch A

Frost forms on the valley floor when the temperature drops below 0 °C.

A Sketch A

Represents a pollution dome at night.

A Sketch A

Pollutants are dispersed.

A Sketch A

Denser concentration of pollutants over the urban area.

A Sketch A
B Sketch B
Refer to the cross-section of a mid-latitude cyclone. In which general direction do mid-latitude cyclones move?
subQuestions.memoText: West to east (1) / Eastwards (1). [ANY ONE] (1 x 1) (1)

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for your answer to QUESTION 1.3.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Driven by the westerlies (2) / Occurs in the westerly wind belt (2). [ANY ONE] (1 x 2) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: How does front A give rise to the formation of cumulonimbus clouds?
subQuestions.memoText: Cold front will undercut the warm air (ahead of it) (2); The steeper gradient will cause rapid uplift of the warm air (2); Cooling and condensation occurs (2). [ANY TWO] (2 x 2) (4)

subQuestions.questionText: In a paragraph of approximately EIGHT lines, explain strategies that can be put in place to manage the negative environmental impact of the heavy rainfall associated with mid-latitude cyclones.
subQuestions.memoText: Maintain natural vegetation (2); Encourage afforestation (2); Buffering of the area (2); Create effective drainage systems (2); Use of sandbags (2); Building of retaining walls (accept examples) (2); Use of catch nets (areas prone to rockfalls) (2); Use of canopies (areas prone to rockfalls) (2); Construction of gabions (2); Construct dams (wall) / weir (2); Construct artificial levees / barriers (2); Conserve wetlands / marshes / swamps (2); Implement contour ploughing (2); Terracing of slopes (2); Widening river channels (water management systems) (2); Canalising rivers (2); Educate people about environmental conservation (2); Awareness / early warning systems (2). [ANY FOUR] (4 x 2) (8)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the infographic based on Tropical Cyclone Filipo. State ONE condition that could have led to the development of Tropical Cyclone Filipo.
subQuestions.memoText: Presence of a low-pressure system / convergence of air (1); Presence of Coriolis force (1); Sea surface temperatures of 26,5 °C or more (1); Calm conditions over the oceans (1); Unstable conditions / high rates of evaporation over the oceans / high humidity (1); Production of latent heat (1); Upper air divergence (1). [ANY ONE] (1 x 1) (1)

subQuestions.questionText: Give evidence from the map and table of information that Tropical Cyclone Filipo had strengthened from 10 to 11 March.
subQuestions.memoText: Exposed to more moisture over the ocean from 10 to 11 March (1); Wind speed increased from 63 km/h to 95 km/h / 116 km/h (1). (2 x 1) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons for the decrease in wind speed from 06:00 to 18:00 on 12 March.
subQuestions.memoText: Moved over the land / less moisture (2); More friction (2); Less latent heat (2); Starting to dissipate (2). [ANY TWO] (2 x 2) (4)

subQuestions.questionText:
On 14 March, Tropical Cyclone Filipo reached the mature stage. Draw a labelled cross-section of Tropical Cyclone Filipo in its mature stage. Marks will be awarded for the following:
(a) Cross-section (1)
(b) Cloud type (1)
(c) Eye (1)
(d) Air movement in the eye (1)
subQuestions.memoText: Sketch: labelled cross-section (1); cloud type (1); eye (1); air movement in the eye (1). (4 x 1) (4)

subQuestions.questionText: Account for the lack of rainfall and clouds in the eye of the tropical cyclone.
subQuestions.memoText: Air subsides (2); The air heats up (2); Moisture gets evaporated / air is dry (2); No condensation takes place (2). [ANY TWO] (2 x 2) (4)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the source based on line thunderstorms. According to the extract, in which season do line thunderstorms commonly occur?
Describe the temperature and moisture content of wind A and wind B that led to the formation of the line thunderstorm.
subQuestions.memoText: WIND A (south-westerly): cold and dry (2). WIND B (north-easterly): warm and moist (2). (2 x 2). INSTRUCTIONS FOR PART MARKING: WIND A (south-westerly) cold (1) or dry (1); WIND B (north-easterly) warm (1) or moist (1). [MAXIMUM OF TWO MARKS] (4)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why the heaviest rainfall occurs closest to the moisture front, as evident in the source.
subQuestions.memoText: Close to the moisture front: Rapid uplift of air along the moisture front (2); Greater (vertical) condensation (2); (Dense line of) cumulonimbus clouds form (2). OR Further from the moisture front: Less uplift of air further from the moisture front (2); Less (vertical) condensation (2); Less clouds form (2). [ANY TWO – MUST REFER TO EITHER CLOSE TO OR FURTHER FROM MOISTURE FRONT] (2 x 2) (4)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the negative physical (natural) impact of line thunderstorms.
subQuestions.memoText: Natural habitats will be destroyed (2); Ecosystems will be destroyed (2); Biodiversity will be reduced (2); Top soil will be washed away / soil erosion (2); Mass movements can be triggered (accept examples) (2); Wildlife would be displaced / drowned (2); Trees / natural vegetation can be uprooted / destroyed (2); Water quality will be reduced (2); Increased leaching of soil (2); Sinkholes form (2); Silting up / deposition of material (2). [ANY THREE] (3 x 2) (6)

subQuestions.questionText:
Match the statement in COLUMN A with the correct option in COLUMN B on drainage basins. Write only Y or Z.

Area drained by a river and its tributaries.

Y catchment area
Z drainage basin

Match the statement in COLUMN A with the correct option in COLUMN B on drainage basins. Write only Y or Z.

Promotes a rapid rise in the water table.

Y gentle gradient
Z steep gradient

Match the statement in COLUMN A with the correct option in COLUMN B on drainage basins. Write only Y or Z.

The upper level of ground water.

Y water table
Z through flow

Match the statement in COLUMN A with the correct option in COLUMN B on drainage basins. Write only Y or Z.

Seepage of water into the ground.

Y infiltration
Z run-off

Match the statement in COLUMN A with the correct option in COLUMN B on drainage basins. Write only Y or Z.

Causes reduction of surface run-off.

Y impermeable rocks
Z dense vegetation

Refer to the sketch of the drainage basin with points Y and Z marked. The confluence is located at Y/Z. Write only Y or Z.

Y point Y on the sketch
Z point Z on the sketch

Refer to the sketch of the drainage basin with points Y and Z marked (KEY: high-lying area, streams). High-lying area separating two tributaries in the same river system. Write only Y or Z.

Y point Y on the sketch
Z point Z on the sketch

Refer to the sketch of the river valley. ... is responsible for the shape of the river valley depicted.

A Deposition
B Lateral erosion
C Weathering
D Vertical erosion

A ... forms at the base of a waterfall.

A braided stream
B delta
C gorge
D plunge pool

The fluvial landform/feature depicted in the sketch is a ...

A waterfall.
B valley.
C rapid.
D cliff.

The flat, low-lying area along the banks of a river in the lower course is a/an ...

A meander.
B delta.
C flood plain.
D alluvial fan.

The slope at X on the inner bank of a meander is also referred to as a/an ... slope.

A steep
B undercut
C concave
D slip-off

A/An ... forms when the meander loop is cut off from the main stream.

A delta
B rapid
C ox-bow lake
D flood plain

The benefit of natural levees is ... on the flood plain.

A increased deposition
B reduced flooding
C reduced fertility
D increased flooding

Deltas form at the river mouth when the following conditions occur:

(i) Shallow sea bed
(ii) Steep sea bed
(iii) Strong currents
(iv) Small tidal range

A (i) and (ii)
B (ii) and (iii)
C (iii) and (iv)
D (i) and (iv)
Refer to drainage patterns A and B. Identify drainage pattern A.
Determine the stream order of X in drainage pattern A.
Give a reason for the direction in which streams flow in drainage pattern A.
subQuestions.memoText: Radiates outwards from a high-lying central point (accept examples of landforms) (2). (1 x 2) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: How does the joining of the tributaries to the mainstream differ in drainage patterns A and B?
subQuestions.memoText: The tributaries join the main river at acute angles at A and at right angles at B (2). (1 x 2) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO conditions associated with the underlying rock that contributed to the formation of trellis drainage pattern B.
subQuestions.memoText: Alternate layers of hard and soft rock (varying resistance) (2); Folded rocks (2). (2 x 2) (4)

subQuestions.questionText: Why are human activities limited in areas where drainage patterns A and B are found?
subQuestions.memoText: Land is steep / uneven (2); Prone to soil erosion / thin soils (2); Infertile soils (2); Risk of mass movements (2); High cost of developing land (2). [ANY TWO] (2 x 2) (4)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the sketch on river rejuvenation. Define the term river rejuvenation.
subQuestions.memoText: When the river experiences an increase in energy (erodes vertically) (2). [CONCEPT] (1 x 2) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the feature at A.
How does feature A indicate that river rejuvenation has taken place?
subQuestions.memoText: Change / drop in gradient (2); Evidence of vertical erosion (2); Water flowing faster (2); Evidence of old and new river profiles (2). [ANY ONE] (1 x 2) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the change that river rejuvenation has made to the landscape at B.
subQuestions.memoText: It formed a valley in a valley (2); The river channel got deeper / steeper / wider (2). [ANY ONE] (1 x 2) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the river terraces in the sketch. How do river terraces form?
subQuestions.memoText: Vertical erosion occurs on the flood plain (2); A new river valley is formed (2); This creates a step-like feature (known as a terrace) (2); The old flood plain is now the river terrace (2). [ANY TWO] (2 x 2) (4)

subQuestions.questionText: Why are some river terraces not suitable for farming?
subQuestions.memoText: Far from water sources (2); Difficult / expensive to build infrastructure (accept examples) (2); River terraces can be very narrow (2); Limit use of machinery (2); Decrease in soil fertility / thin soils (2); Uneven slopes / rugged landscape (2); Unstable soil / mass movement (accept examples) (2). [ANY TWO] (2 x 2) (4)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the extract on catchment and river management. What is river management?
subQuestions.memoText: Monitoring and controlling (management) of water resources in a drainage basin / catchment area (2). [CONCEPT] (1 x 2) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Name ONE human activity in the extract that has a negative impact on South Africa's catchment areas.
How does the human activity (answer to QUESTION 2.5.2) negatively impact the health (water quality) of a catchment area?
subQuestions.memoText: Causes eutrophication / reduction in oxygen levels (2); Imbalance in the nutrient levels in the river (2); Reduction in biodiversity (2); Reduction in fauna and flora (2); Water pollution (accept examples) (2); Increase in water borne diseases (2); Ecosystems / natural habitats are disrupted (2); Water table will be lowered (2); Increase in soil erosion (2). [ANY TWO] (2 x 2) (4)

subQuestions.questionText: In a paragraph of approximately EIGHT lines, suggest sustainable strategies the government can put in place to preserve river catchment areas.
subQuestions.memoText: Educational programmes (2); Awareness programmes (accept examples) (2); Implement legislation / laws / conservation zones (accept examples) (2); Impose fines (2); Improve waste water / grey water treatment (2); Create buffer zones (accept examples) (2); Encourage afforestation (2); Remove alien vegetation (2); Proper sewerage / water purification systems (2); Maximise wastewater / grey water usage (2); Frequent testing of water (2); Conserve wetlands (2); Recycle agricultural / domestic / industrial waste (2); Maintain / construct water infrastructure (2); Sustainable farming (accept examples) (2); Encourage rain water harvesting (2). [ANY FOUR] (4 x 2) (8)

subQuestions.questionText:
MAP SKILLS AND CALCULATIONS. Refer to the 1 : 50 000 topographical map 2829DB LADYSMITH. The town closest to Ladysmith is ...

A Glencoe.
B Harrismith.
C Newcastle.
D Colenso.

The feature located at grid reference (coordinates) 28°31'32"S and 29°47'22"E is ...

A cultivated land.
B perennial water.
C a road.
D a reservoir.

The mean magnetic declination for the year ... was 21°03' west of true north.

A 2000
B 1995
C 2001
D 2024
Determine the total annual change for 2024. Show ALL calculations.

Refer to the orthophoto map. Calculate the area of the demarcated feature 6 in blocks A4/A5 and block B4. Give the answer in km². Use the following information: Length is 3,0 cm. Formula: Length x Breadth. Show ALL calculations.
Give a reason why the expansion of the demarcated feature 6 (answer to QUESTION 3.1.5) is limited in a south-easterly direction.
subQuestions.memoText: Due to the river (1); Row of trees forms a buffer zone (1); There is a recreational area (accept greenbelt) (1). [ANY ONE] (1 x 1) (1)

subQuestions.label: 3.2.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText: MAP INTERPRETATION. Refer to F in block C2 and G in block D4 on the topographical map. The temperature at F in the centre of the town is 2 °C higher than at G. Name the concept that describes this difference.

subQuestions.label: 3.2.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE reason why the high density of buildings at F generally contributes to the higher temperatures.
subQuestions.memoText: Heat will get trapped (2); Reduced wind speed (2); Reduced air flow (2); Artificial surfaces (2); Multiple reflections (2). [ANY ONE] (1 x 2) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to blocks D2 and D3 on the orthophoto map. Explain how aspect of slope determined the location of Rose Park at 7 on the orthophoto map.
subQuestions.memoText: Rose Park at 7 is located on the north(east)-facing slope which is warmer / receives more insolation (2). (1 x 2). INSTRUCTIONS FOR PART MARKING: Rose Park at 7 is located on the north(east)-facing slope (1). [MAXIMUM 1 MARK] (2)

subQuestions.questionText:
Refer to the dam H in block B1 on the topographical map. The dam wall indicates that the river is flowing in a ... direction.

A south-westerly
B north-easterly
C north-westerly
D south-easterly
Refer to the weir at I in block A3 on the topographical map. A weir is used to regulate (control) the flow of water in a river. Explain why the construction of the weir was necessary.
subQuestions.memoText: To reduce the risk of flooding due to the confluence of rivers (2); To reduce the risk of flooding downstream (cultivated land, built-up area, railway line, caravan park) (2). [ANY ONE] (1 x 2). INSTRUCTIONS FOR PART MARKING: To reduce the risk of flooding (1). [MAXIMUM 1 MARK] (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the section of the Klip River from 8 in block A2 to 9 in block A5 on the orthophoto map. Identify the fluvial landform/feature.
Give evidence why this fluvial landform/feature (answer to QUESTION 3.2.5) developed in this area.
subQuestions.memoText: Land is flat / gentle (accept lower course) (1); Contour lines are far apart (1). [ANY ONE] (1 x 1) (1)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to block C5 on the orthophoto map. Why will more erosion take place at 11 than at 10?
subQuestions.memoText: Water flows faster on the outer bank / 11 / undercut slope (2); Water flows slower on the inner bank / 10 / slip-off slope (2). [ANY ONE] (1 x 2) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: GEOGRAPHICAL INFORMATION SYSTEMS (GIS). The vertical aerial photograph used to make the orthophoto map has a (high/low) resolution.
The reference of the topographical map represents (spatial/attribute) data.
How does this data (answer to QUESTION 3.3.2) assist in identifying feature J on the topographical map?
subQuestions.memoText: It indicates what feature J represents in reality (2); The reference shows that the symbol at J is an excavation (2); To distinguish between similar land-use features (mine dump and mine excavation) (2). [ANY ONE] (1 x 2) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to 12 in block C2 on the orthophoto map. Define the term buffering.
subQuestions.memoText: The demarcation of an area around / along a geographical feature / location (2). [CONCEPT] (1 x 2) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: How would buffering at 12 protect the quality of the water in the Klip River?
subQuestions.memoText: Restrict development on the banks of the river (2); Decrease pollution from the built-up area (2); Reduces eroded soil from entering the river (2); Decreased eutrophication (2); Reduces salinity (2); The natural course / capacity of the river will be maintained (2); Biodiversity of the river will be preserved (2). [ANY ONE] (1 x 2) (2)
